papers.title: The CFDE Workbench: Integrating Metadata and Processed Data from Common Fund Programs.
papers.abstract: The NIH Common Fund Data Ecosystem (CFDE) program was established to facilitate data accessibility and interoperability across multiple Common Fund (CF) programs, promote collaborations and accelerate discoveries by combining diverse data types from different CF programs. The CFDE Data Resource Center (DRC) was tasked with developing two web-based portals: an Information Portal to serve information about the CFDE, and a Data Portal to host harmonized metadata and processed data contributed by participating CF Data Coordination Centers (DCCs) and other sources. To achieve these goals, the CFDE
papers.summary: The CFDE Workbench is a web-based platform that integrates harmonized metadata and processed data from multiple NIH Common Fund programs, enabling cross-program data discovery and interoperability. It provides an Information Portal for program details and a Data Portal for querying contributed datasets, aiming to accelerate discoveries by combining diverse data types.

papers.title: PDBe-KB Complexes: Enabling Functional Insight from Macromolecular Complexes in the PDB.
papers.abstract: PDBe-KB Complexes is a set of webpages that aggregate experimentally determined macromolecular assemblies into unique complex-level records within the Protein Data Bank in Europe Knowledge Base framework. Each unique complex identifier unifies equivalent biological assemblies from the PDB that represent the same macromolecular complex, consolidating information on component identity, stoichiometry, symmetry, ligands, and PISA-derived assembly properties within a consistent framework. Relationships between complexes are established by comparing their compositions, capturing both subcomplexes th
papers.summary: PDBe-KB Complexes is a new resource that groups equivalent macromolecular assemblies from the PDB into unified complex-level records, consolidating data on component identity, stoichiometry, symmetry, ligands, and assembly properties. It also captures relationships between complexes, such as subcomplexes, providing a consistent framework for functional interpretation of protein assemblies.

papers.title: Utilization of advanced machine learning based on financial ontology induction for adaptive multilingual method in document recognition.
papers.abstract: A noise-robust framework is introduced for semi-supervised cross-lingual financial ontology induction, designed to address the challenges posed by noisy and partially labeled multilingual financial documents. The method employs a confidence-based filtering mechanism to eliminate low-quality cross-lingual text pairs, followed by multi-view distillation to harmonize linguistic and structural representations of financial entities. An uncertainty-aware contrastive learning objective further aligns entities across languages while reducing the influence of unreliable alignments. The resulting ontolo
papers.summary: The paper presents a semi-supervised machine learning framework for inducing financial ontologies across multiple languages from noisy, partially labeled documents. It uses confidence-based filtering, multi-view distillation, and uncertainty-aware contrastive learning to align financial entities across languages despite unreliable data. The result is a more noise-robust multilingual ontology induction method.

papers.title: Integrated Single Cell Analysis Reveals the Transcriptional Heterogeneity of Mouse Double Negative T Cells.
papers.abstract: Double negative T cells (DNT cells) are a rare T cell population involved in immune regulation, inflammation, autoimmunity, transplantation, and tumor immunity. However, their low abundance and dispersed distribution across tissues have limited a systematic understanding of their cellular organization and transcriptional diversity. To address this problem, we developed an integrative single cell framework to reconstruct the mouse DNT cell landscape across tissues using multiple public single cell RNA sequencing datasets. Using transcriptomic criteria, we identified and integrated 7984 mouse RN
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple public single-cell RNA-seq datasets to reconstruct the transcriptional landscape of rare mouse double negative T (DNT) cells across tissues, identifying 7,984 cells for analysis. The authors reveal previously unappreciated transcriptional heterogeneity within this low-abundance immune population, providing a systematic framework for studying DNT cell organization.

papers.title: Programmatic access to ICTV virus taxonomy through a public ontology API.
papers.abstract: The International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV) is responsible for developing and maintaining a universal virus taxonomy. As the reference framework for organising the viral world, it is essential for virology and related fields. Despite its widespread use in research and public health, programmatic access to ICTV taxonomy has remained limited, posing challenges for integration, versioning, and interoperability across databases and bioinformatics resources requiring up-to-date virus taxonomy.
papers.summary: The authors present a public ontology API that provides programmatic access to the ICTV virus taxonomy, addressing the previous lack of machine-readable, versioned access. This enables databases and bioinformatics pipelines to integrate up-to-date virus taxonomy directly, improving interoperability across virology and public health resources.

papers.title: Association mapping for canopy temperature under irrigated and rainfed conditions at 12 environments identified both known and novel genetic loci.
papers.abstract: Soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merrill) is the most widely cultivated oilseed crop and faces significant yield challenges due to drought stress. Canopy temperature has been proposed as an effective proxy for evaluation of differences in genotypic responses to water limitation, as well as indirectly assessing transpiration and stomatal conductance. Cooler canopy temperatures are associated with higher transpiration and open stomata, whereas warmer canopy temperatures are associated with reduced transpiration and stomatal closure. This study evaluated a diverse group of 205 soybean maturity group IV
papers.summary: This study performed association mapping in 205 diverse soybean lines across 12 environments to identify genetic loci linked to canopy temperature, a proxy for drought tolerance. The analysis uncovered both previously known and novel loci associated with canopy temperature under irrigated and rainfed conditions, providing candidate targets for breeding drought-resilient soybean.

papers.title: From knowledge graph to topological data analysis: a novel framework to analyze gene regulatory networks for tomato-multi-pathogen interactions.
papers.abstract: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum), despite being the most important vegetable crop world-wide, remains vulnerable to over 200 diseases caused by different pests. Although tomato molecular response to individual stresses is well studied, the gene regulatory network (GRN) representing the crosstalk and trade-offs of multi-stress responses remains almost unexplored. We developed GENIAL (Gene rEgulatory Network and topologIcal datA anaLysis) to refine and analyze complex GRNs and TomTom, a knowledge graph that gathers 11 publicly available databases in a unique FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperabl
papers.summary: The authors developed GENIAL, a framework combining gene regulatory network (GRN) refinement with topological data analysis, and TomTom, a FAIR knowledge graph integrating 11 public databases, to study tomato responses to multiple pathogens. This enables exploration of crosstalk and trade-offs in multi-stress gene regulation, which was previously uncharacterized in tomato.

papers.title: iMPI: An Integrative Database for MicroProteins Encoded by Intron Retention in Tumors.
papers.abstract: Research advancements made in the last decade have shed light on the dysregulation of cellular mechanisms that lead to aberrant and pathologic intron retention (IR). IR is not merely a mechanism of gene regulation but may also play a potential role in cancer pathogenesis and therapeutic resistance across various human cancers. Despite its potential significance, there remains a notable gap in comprehensive database resources for introns within tumors. Therefore, we investigated whether the retained introns contain undiscovered protein-coding ORFs and whether they can encode proteins. We conduc
papers.summary: This paper introduces iMPI, an integrative database cataloging microproteins that could be encoded by retained introns in tumors. The authors systematically investigated whether retained introns contain undiscovered protein-coding ORFs and whether these can produce proteins, addressing a gap in tumor-focused intron resources. The database aims to support research into the role of intron retention in cancer pathogenesis and therapeutic resistance.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Model-Informed Drug Development: Augmentation, Acceleration, and Regulatory Preparation.
papers.abstract: The convergence of MIDD and AI represents a natural evolution from established quantitative frameworks toward a broader, more powerful computational toolbox that can address persistent MIDD challenges such as high-dimensional data integration, complex biology, and operational constraints in evidence generation. AI can both enhance traditional MIDD through hybrid approaches and extend MIDD's horizon to include various AI models. Recent publications of guidance demonstrate the agency's preparation on the acceptance of AI in MIDD.
papers.summary: This paper reviews how artificial intelligence is being integrated into model-informed drug development (MIDD), both by enhancing existing quantitative pharmacology approaches and by enabling new AI-driven models. It highlights that regulatory agencies are preparing guidance for accepting AI in MIDD, signaling a shift toward broader computational toolboxes for drug development.

papers.title: Multimodality, interaction modeling, and multimodule architectures in genomic prediction: A unified conceptual framework.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of genomic, environmental, phenomic, and other high-dimensional data sources has transformed genomic prediction in plant breeding. However, the terms multimodal, interaction modeling, and multimodule architecture are often used inconsistently, generating ambiguity regarding whether they refer to biological assumptions, data integration strategies, or computational design. These dimensions are conceptually independent in the sense that none logically requires or implies the others. Interaction modeling may be implemented within a multimodule architecture, but modular computa
papers.summary: This paper proposes a unified conceptual framework to clarify three often-conflated terms in genomic prediction for plant breeding: multimodality (integrating diverse data types), interaction modeling (capturing non-additive effects like epistasis), and multimodule architectures (modular computational designs). The authors argue these dimensions are conceptually independent, and that clearer terminology would reduce ambiguity in how biological assumptions, data integration strategies, and computational designs are described and compared.

papers.title: Mapping ovarian cellular and molecular landscape across the lifespan of women: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: With growing interest in ART, fertility preservation, and postmenopausal health of women, reproductive medicine is increasingly focused on characterizing oocytes and ovarian tissue composition, as well as understanding the molecular mechanisms that guide ovarian function throughout its lifecycle. High-throughput omics technologies have enabled the characterization of different molecular layers, leading to substantial advances in our understanding of their complex dynamics. However, not all molecular aspects are studied equally, and studies examining the same modalities often show inconsistenci
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the existing high-throughput omics literature on the human ovary across the female lifespan, covering oocytes and ovarian tissue composition. It finds that molecular layers are studied unevenly and that studies of the same modalities often report inconsistent results, highlighting gaps and the need for standardization in reproductive omics research.

papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence in animal genomics for smart agriculture: Applications, challenges, and future prospects.
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a groundbreaking paradigm in the field of animal genomics and is providing the possibility to take a step towards intelligent agriculture, with better data integration, predictive modeling, and biological design. This review focuses on the shift from predictive to generative modelling paradigms, examining their implications for data synthesis, biological sequence design, and integrative smart livestock systems. It provides a comprehensive overview of recent developments, applications, and challenges at the intersection of generative AI and an
papers.summary: This review surveys how generative AI is being applied to animal genomics, moving beyond predictive modeling toward data synthesis, biological sequence design, and integrated smart livestock systems. It catalogs recent developments, applications, and challenges at the intersection of generative AI and animal breeding for smart agriculture.

papers.title: Re-emerging Marburg virus disease in Africa: spillover ecology, geographic expansion, and surveillance vulnerabilities.
papers.abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD) is re-emerging across Africa as a high-consequence zoonosis shaped by expanding ecological suitability, repeated spillover, and uneven surveillance capacity. This review synthesizes current evidence on the ecological, epidemiological, and operational determinants of contemporary Marburg virus (MARV) emergence. We conceptualize MVD as an ecological-emergence system produced by interactions among reservoir-host biology, environmental change, human exposure, health-system readiness, and mobility, rather than as a series of isolated outbreaks. Recent detections in multi
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the re-emergence of Marburg virus disease across Africa, framing outbreaks as an ecological-emergence system driven by reservoir-host biology, environmental change, human exposure, health-system readiness, and mobility. It highlights expanding ecological suitability, repeated spillovers, and uneven surveillance capacity as key determinants of contemporary Marburg virus emergence.

papers.title: Functional mapping of the Trypanosoma cruzi serinome by fluorophosphonate activity-based protein profiling.
papers.abstract: Serine hydrolases (SHs) constitute one of the largest enzyme superfamilies in eukaryotes, yet their roles in Trypanosoma cruzi, the causative agent of Chagas disease, remain largely uncharacterized. Here, we report an activity-based chemoproteomic map of the T. cruzi epimastigote serinome by combining genome-informed in silico curation with whole-cell activity-based protein profiling (ABPP) using a panel of cell-permeable fluorophosphonate (FP)-alkyne probes. Whole-cell labelling followed by label-free quantitative proteomics (LFQ-MS) identified 37 enriched SH-like proteins, including 35 with
papers.summary: This study maps the active serine hydrolase enzymes (the 'serinome') of Trypanosoma cruzi, the parasite that causes Chagas disease, using fluorophosphonate activity-based probes combined with quantitative proteomics. The authors identified 37 enriched serine hydrolase-like proteins in the epimastigote stage, providing a functional enzyme inventory that could inform drug target discovery. This represents one of the first activity-based chemoproteomic surveys of this understudied parasite.

papers.title: An Ontology for Workplace Violence: Protocol to support Cross-sector Incident Reporting in Public Services.
papers.abstract: Underreporting is a defining problem in the registration of workplace violence across public services. This is reinforced by inconsistent, often poor incident descriptions and the absence of a clear, shared nomenclature. Without an ontology-backed structure, similar events are recorded differently across settings or remain uncodable and effectively invisible. Moreover, WPV is typically registered and studied within sector- and even organization-specific categories and local reporting logics rather than through a shared semantic framework, limiting comparability and cumulative understanding acr
papers.summary: This protocol paper proposes developing an ontology to standardize how workplace violence incidents are described and coded across public services. The goal is to address chronic underreporting caused by inconsistent terminology and sector-specific reporting practices, enabling better comparability and cumulative analysis across settings.

papers.title: Candidate metabolites in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Network analysis and in vitro validation of glycitein.
papers.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis. Cerebrovascular endothelial injury serves as a key contributor to its pathogenesis, and metabolite-mediated inflammatory regulation may be involved in this process. However, the specific candidate metabolites and their underlying pathways remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to identify candidate metabolites related to SAE through network pharmacology and to provide preliminary in vitro validation.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology to identify candidate metabolites linked to sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), focusing on cerebrovascular endothelial injury and inflammation. The authors provide preliminary in vitro validation of glycitein as a potential protective metabolite. The work highlights a possible metabolite-based mechanism in SAE pathogenesis.

papers.title: Spatial omics illuminates tumor heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) is the coexistence of diverse cancer cell states, genotypes, and microenvironmental niches within a single tumor and is a major driver of therapeutic resistance and disease progression. While the clinical implications of ITH are well appreciated, conventional methods and models have been limited in resolving the spatial and functional complexity underlying ITH. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics, high-plex imaging, and in vivo CRISPR perturbation and lineage tracing now enable unprecedented, mechanistic dissection of tumor ecosystems. These techno
papers.summary: This review discusses how recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics, high-plex imaging, and in vivo CRISPR perturbation and lineage tracing are enabling mechanistic dissection of intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH). It highlights how these technologies overcome limitations of conventional methods in resolving the spatial and functional complexity of tumor ecosystems that drive therapeutic resistance and disease progression.

papers.title: A multi-agent GraphRAG framework for pharmacotherapy safety verification in clinical decision support systems.
papers.abstract: The management of pharmacotherapy in patients with multimorbidity and polypharmacy is a difficult task in routine clinical practice. Clinicians must consider diagnoses, prescribed drugs, contraindications, drug-drug interactions, renal and hepatic function, laboratory values, dose limits and individual risk factors. Clinical decision support systems in traditional settings are based on static rules, and hard to update. Standalone large language models are capable of processing clinical language but their outputs may be unsupported by evidence, incomplete or out of date. In this study, we devel
papers.summary: This paper presents a multi-agent GraphRAG framework that combines knowledge graphs with large language models to verify pharmacotherapy safety in clinical decision support. The system addresses polypharmacy and multimorbidity by integrating diagnoses, drug interactions, contraindications, organ function, and lab values, overcoming the limitations of static rule-based systems and standalone LLMs. It aims to provide evidence-grounded, up-to-date safety checks for medication management.

papers.title: Piecewise latent growth modeling as the methodological standard for evaluation research.
papers.abstract: Evaluation research across applied domains-clinical intervention, psychotherapy, curriculum reform, organizational change-has long relied on the pre-post difference score as its primary evidence of change. This paper argues that this reliance reflects not merely a methodological habit but a systematic ontological error: the implicit treatment of change as a discrete event rather than a continuous, phase-structured process. We develop a theoretical and methodological case for piecewise latent growth modeling (PLGM) as the appropriate evaluative standard across these domains. Drawing on classica
papers.summary: This paper argues that evaluation research should move beyond simple pre-post difference scores, which treat change as a discrete event, and instead adopt piecewise latent growth modeling (PLGM) to capture change as a continuous, phase-structured process. The authors provide a theoretical and methodological case for PLGM as the standard across clinical, educational, and organizational evaluation contexts.

papers.title: A practical guide to functional enrichment analysis.
papers.abstract: Functional Enrichment Analysis (FEA) has become a critical step in the analysis of omics data in recent years. As a result, numerous approaches have been rapidly developed, leading to an overflow of information that can be difficult for beginners to navigate. Most usage information on FEA methods is scattered across countless articles that often address specific problems, making it difficult to find practical recommendations and good practices. In these guidelines, we discuss the current landscape of FEA and FEA-related approaches and organize actionable knowledge to support first-timers and u
papers.summary: This paper provides a practical guide to functional enrichment analysis (FEA), a widely used approach for interpreting omics data by identifying biological functions, pathways, or processes that are over-represented in a gene or protein list. It surveys the current landscape of FEA methods and consolidates scattered best practices and actionable recommendations into a single resource aimed at beginners and newcomers to the field.

papers.title: Comparative transcriptomic analysis of functional and metabolic changes in mass-reared and wild Anastrepha ludens Loew (Diptera: Tephritidae).
papers.abstract: Mass rearing for the Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) may induce transcriptomic changes that influence post-release performance. We compared head transcriptomes of two mass-reared Anastrepha ludens strains, Bisexual and Tap-7, with wild individuals associated with their preferred natural host, sweet orange.
papers.summary: This study compared head transcriptomes of mass-reared versus wild Anastrepha ludens fruit flies, finding functional and metabolic gene expression differences that may affect performance after sterile insect technique release. The results highlight how domestication under mass rearing can reshape gene expression in ways relevant to pest control programs.

papers.title: Highly contiguous reference genome assembly of the endangered Orcés' blue whiptail Holcosus orcesi.
papers.abstract: Holcosus orcesi, the Orcés' Blue Whiptail, is a Critically Endangered lizard endemic to the upper Jubones River basin in southern Ecuador. Restricted to a narrow elevational range within semi-arid Andean shrublands, it represents one of the few montane members of a predominantly lowland lineage. Here we present the first high-quality reference genome for H. orcesi, generated using Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read sequencing. The assembly spans 1.68 Gb across only 91 contigs, with an N50 of 76.2 Mb and a BUSCO completeness of 96.8%, making it among the most contiguous and complete squamat
papers.summary: This paper presents the first high-quality reference genome for Holcosus orcesi, a critically endangered Andean lizard, assembled using Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing. The 1.68 Gb assembly is highly contiguous (91 contigs, N50 of 76.2 Mb) and 96.8% complete by BUSCO, making it one of the most contiguous squamate genomes to date. This resource will support conservation genomics and evolutionary studies of this rare montane lineage.

papers.title: The data substrate of exposome intelligence: an interoperability profile for untargeted metabolomics.
papers.abstract: Untargeted metabolomics, anchored in high-resolution mass spectrometry, has matured into the central analytical platform of human exposomics. It can capture endogenous biology, diet, drugs, microbial chemistry, environmental contaminants, and their transformation products from a single biological sample. Yet exposome science remains stubbornly single-study: most untargeted exposomics publications stand alone, featuring tables, partial annotations, and semi-quantitative intensities that cannot be combined across cohorts. The bottleneck is no longer instrumentation or annotation; it is interoper
papers.summary: This perspective argues that untargeted metabolomics, the core analytical platform for human exposomics, is limited not by instrumentation or annotation but by poor data interoperability. Most exposomics studies remain single-study silos with incompatible tables and semi-quantitative intensities, preventing cross-cohort integration. The authors propose an interoperability profile to make exposomics data combinable and reusable.
